input.title: Claudinite canon: rule revalidation
input.head: claudinite/claudinite-canon-curation/canon-rule-revalidation/2026-09-27-elek5q
input.body:
Re-probed the `packs/` shelf's environmental claims — the ones falsified by a change nobody in this repo makes — and corrected the four that no longer hold. Every verdict below carries the probe behind it; a reviewer cannot re-derive any of this from the diff.

Corpus: `packs/` (the shelf; this pack declares no `write_paths`, so there is no second root).

Refs #2349

## stale (corrected) — 4 claims, 3 elements

**1. `git-github-advanced`: "`get_job_logs(run_id, failed_only: true)` — '0 failed jobs' means green"**

Probe: run `36313686047` in this repo, while `actions_get`/`get_workflow_run` reported `status: "in_progress"` and its only job was `in_progress`:

```
get_job_logs(run_id: 36313686047, failed_only: true)
→ {"failed_jobs":0,"message":"No failed jobs found in this workflow run","run_id":36313686047,"total_jobs":1}
```

A running run answers identically to a green one, so the section's stated way to confirm a non-PR run reads an unfinished job as passed. Corrected to name the run's own `status`/`conclusion` as the confirmation, and to say what zero failures actually means.

**2. `git-github-advanced`: "it 404s for a job still `in_progress`"**

Probe: job `108604274914` of that same run, `status: "in_progress"`:

```
get_job_logs(job_id: 108604274914, tail_lines: 5)
→ {"job_id":…,"logs_url":"https://productionresultssa19.blob.core.windows.net/…","message":"Job logs are available for download"}

get_job_logs(job_id: 108604274914, tail_lines: 8, return_content: true)
→ failed to get job logs: … failed to download logs: HTTP 404
```

The call does not 404 — it hands back a `logs_url` and a success message. Only `return_content: true` surfaces the 404. Corrected to say which form tells the truth.

**3. `basics/repo-text-sweeps`: "The tool-results paths are harness-internal and inaccessible to shell commands"**

Probe:

```
$ head -c 300 /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-Claudinite/<session>.jsonl
{"type":"queue-operation","operation":"enqueue","timestamp":"2026-09-27T10:51:20.388Z",…}
```

The shell reads those paths fine. A `python3` pass over the file counts typed JSONL entries (`attachment`, `user`, `assistant`, …), which is the real reason a `cp` is wrong: it yields escaped JSON records, not the captured output. The directive stands; its reason was wrong, and the wrong reason is the half a reader acts on.

**4. `aws-sam` `reach-aws-session`: "point it at the sandbox proxy's CA bundle (`AWS_CA_BUNDLE`) if a call fails TLS verification"**

Probe: the sandbox already exports it, alongside three siblings —

```
AWS_CA_BUNDLE=[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
SSL_CERT_FILE=[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
```

The remedy was a no-op, which sends a TLS failure down a dead path. The rule's other half re-probed true: `which aws sam` exits 1 and `import boto3` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`.

## holds — 19 claims

| claim | probe |
|---|---|
| `basics` `calling-edit-path` — outside root refuses without a session read | shell-written `/home/user/probe-*.txt`, `Edit` → `File has not been read yet` |
| …inside the working directory needs nothing | shell-written repo file, `Edit` → applied |
| …inside the scratchpad needs nothing | shell-written scratchpad file, `Edit` → applied |
| …a narrow offset window satisfies it | `Read` line 1 only, then `Edit` line 2 → applied |
| …a session `Write` satisfies it | `Write` a new outside file, `Edit` → applied |
| `basics` `select-takes-short` | `select:get_teams` → returned `mcp__github__get_teams` |
| `basics` `bare-short-name` | bare `get_team_members` → returned that tool, ranked first |
| `git-github-advanced` — `get_job_logs` rejects a bare `run_id` | `job_id is required when failed_only is false`, verbatim |
| `git-github-advanced` — a run artifact's blob URL is denied at CONNECT | `curl` of a `*.blob.core.windows.net` logs URL → `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` |
| `git-github-advanced` — the proxy authenticates `api.github.com` as the session, so an in-scope repo answers 200 unauthenticated | `curl https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite` → 200, no `Authorization` header |
| `git-github-advanced` — the unscoped `/rate_limit` and `/user` answer 200 in the same session | both → 200 |
| `git-github-advanced` — `pull_request_read get_status` reads pending/0 for passed Actions CI | PR #2358 → `{"state":"pending","total_count":0,"statuses":[]}` while `get_check_runs` → `test-and-conformance`, `conclusion: success` |
| `git-github-advanced` — `issue_read`'s `get_*` set is split on a PR number | #2358: `get` returned the pull request; `get_labels` → `Could not resolve to an Issue with the number of 2358.` |
| `git-github-advanced` — `list_pull_requests`' `merged` can't be trusted | five squash-merged PRs (#2359, #2358, #2343, #2340, #2321) all `merged: false`, `state: closed` |
| `git-github-advanced` — qualify the `head` filter as `owner:branch` | `missingbulb:claudinite/claudinite-tasks/tasks-usage-fold/2026-09-27-rmmiy6` → exactly PR #2358 |
| `git-github-advanced` — an MCP search layer matches semantically and honours no qualifier | `in:title "canon-rule-revalidation"` returned #2348 and #2142, whose titles say `canon-prose-to-checks` |
| `basics/verify-in-production` — `sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the parent, `sub_issue_id` an id not a number | schema read: `issue_number` "The number of the parent issue"; `sub_issue_id` "ID is not the same as issue number" |
| `basics/do-later` — the mark goes on through `issue_write`'s `labels` | schema read: `labels` array on `issue_write` |
| `claudinite-lifecycle` `finding-mounted-skill` | `.claudinite/shared/skills` does not exist; the `Skill` tool announced `.claude/skills/<name>/` three times this session, and that directory holds only its one `SKILL.md` |
| `node` `throwaway-script-imports` | same ESM script importing a repo-local dependency: inside the project → resolved; in the harness scratchpad → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; with `NODE_PATH` set at that `node_modules` → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` still |
| `node` `relying-version-gated` | session Node is `v22.22.2`; `ci.yml` pins `node-version: 20` and the scheduler/executor/pack-versions workflows pin `24` — the session matches neither |
| growth tasks — "the unattended run carries no `gh` CLI" | `which gh` → not found (`hub` too); `curl`, `node`, `python3` present |
| `claude-code-web-users-support` README — the harness names a web session's person by email only, and carries an attended flag | `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0` are set; no login variable exists |

## doc-verified — 1

`git-github-advanced`'s claim that an MCP layer in front of issue search matches semantically is now stated by the tool itself: `search_issues`' schema description reads "Search issues using natural-language semantic matching… Already scoped to `is:issue`." The live probe above agrees.

## unprobed — 6, each left exactly as it stands

- **`adopt-claudinite`: "one batched `AskUserQuestion` pass (up to 4 per call)".** The tool is absent from an unattended session — `select:AskUserQuestion` found nothing, and a keyword search returned only the task tools. Absence here is not evidence about an attended session.
- **growth-extract / growth-dedup: "its `GITHUB_TOKEN` holds a proxy placeholder a presence test passes on and the API refuses".** The probe (a `curl` carrying the token) was refused by the harness as credential materialization — a policy boundary, not a result. The variable *is* set, which is the half the rule warns about; whether the API refuses it stays unprobed.
- **`git-github-advanced`: a bare `head` filter returns an unrelated PR.** This repo's own `pull-request-head-unqualified` action guard blocked the bare call, so the failing form cannot be exercised here. The qualified remedy probed true (above).
- **`git-github-advanced`: an out-of-scope repo 403s with `GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session.`** Probing it means reading a repository outside this session's granted scope; not done.
- **`git-github-advanced`: `search_code`'s index lags a repo's content.** Needs a cross-repo sweep to measure; outside this session's scope.
- **`git-github` `issue-labels-overwrite`.** Its probe is a label write; read-only probing cannot reach it.

## Not reached

Most of the shelf is judgment prose and out of scope by the skill's test. Of what is in scope, the platform-facing packs whose probes need a driven runtime or a live external service went unprobed this run and are named here so the gap is explicit: `headless-browser`, `host-page`, `chrome-extension`, `web-speech`, `leaflet`, `github-pages`, `cloudflare-site`, `cloudflare-workers`, `firebase`, `google-identity`, `android`, `ios`, `flutter`, `play-store-release`, `app-store-release`, `web-scraping`. The run ordered its budget by what staleness costs, so the always-loaded `basics` contracts and the GitHub/MCP tool surface came first.

## Checks

Whole suite green (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`): one failure surfaced and was fixed — the `aws-sam` edit pushed its rule from 99 to 102 words, past the README's `<100` band, so the rule was tightened back rather than the band restated. `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` both report **0 blocking**. One advisory stands on `git-github-advanced:168`: `no-new-long-dashes` sees the whole edited line, and its remaining long dash belongs to the pre-existing `add_repo` sentence — the claim this run could not probe, so its text was left alone.

Per the task: no pack version bumped and no `VERSIONS.md` row written; both are derived on the base branch after this lands.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.title: github-api-via-shell's message says every repo-scoped api.github.com call 403s; an in-scope repo answers 200
input.body:
The `github-api-via-shell` action guard in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/declared-checks.json` blocks a shell GitHub read with this reason:

> there is no gh CLI here, and every repo-scoped api.github.com call 403s ("GitHub access is not enabled for this session"), so a shell poll reports "still running" until it times out.

The first clause holds — `which gh` exits 1. The second does not, for a repo **in** the session's scope. Probed in this session (work item #2349), unauthenticated, no `Authorization` header of its own:

```
https://api.github.com/repos/missingbulb/Claudinite  -> http=200
https://api.github.com/rate_limit                    -> http=200
https://api.github.com/user                          -> http=200
```

The canon's `git-github-advanced` skill already carries the accurate version: the sandbox's egress proxy authenticates `api.github.com` as the session's own GitHub identity, so an **in-scope** repo answers 200 while an **out-of-scope** one 403s with `GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session. Use add_repo to request access.`

The guard's directive is right either way — read check runs through the MCP tools, not a `curl` poll — and the 403-on-an-out-of-scope-repo failure mode is real. Only its stated reason overreaches, by claiming of every repo-scoped call what is true only of an out-of-scope one. A session that has just probed the 200 reads the message as false and has no way to tell which half to trust.

Suggested fix: narrow the reason to the out-of-scope case, and keep the "reports still running until it times out" consequence attached to it — that is the failure the guard exists to prevent.

This was found by the `canon-rule-revalidation` task, whose corpus is `packs/` only; `.claudinite/local/packs/` is outside it, so the run could not make the change itself.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```
